title: Jolt Physics job system exceeded maximum number of jobs using MultiMeshInstance3D
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: v4.6.2.stable - Not tested in earlier versions. ### System information Godot v4.6.2.stable - Windows 11 (build 22631) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated Intel(R) UHD Graphics (Intel Corporation; 30.0.100.9864) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-1035G1 CPU @ 1.00GHz (8 threads) - 7.74 GiB memory ### Issue description I am attempting to create a simple procedural 3D blocky sandbox world generator using a MultiMeshInstance3D loop along with a basic physics CharacterBody3D player cube on Windows 11 using Godot v4.6.2.stable. During initialization at runtime, the engine completely freezes its worker thread allocation tables and drops this critical console error inside the debugger window: "CreateJob: Jolt Physics job system exceeded the maximum number of jobs. This should not happen. Please report this. Waiting for jobs to become available..." It appears that running physics vector transform updates across thousands of procedural block instances inside a single initialization frame completely overflows the default job queues of the Jolt Physics system in the newest 4.6.2 build when running on a dedicated GTX 970. Images showing the error: ### Steps to reproduce ### Steps to reproduce To reproduce this critical multithreaded Jolt Physics queue crash, follow these exact click-by-click steps inside the engine editor interface layout: 1. Launch Godot Engine v4.6.2.stable on a computer running Windows 11 with following: Windows 11 (build 22631) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated Intel(R) UHD Graphics (Intel Corporation; 30.0.100.9864) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-1035G1 CPU @ 1.00GHz (8 threads) - 7.74 GiB memory 2. Inside the initial Project Manager dashboard wizard screen, click the "New Project" button layout on the right-hand menu sidebar. 3. Type "jolt-thread-crash-test" into the project name box, choose a clean local directory path (e.g., C:\Users\Austin\folder\projects), click "Create Folder", select the "Forward+" (Vulkan Advanced 3D) renderer option bullet, and click "Create & Edit" to launch the main viewport interface. 4. Look at the top-left "Scene" panel column layout window. Left-click the button option that says "3D Scene". This will instantly instantiate a single root spatial parent node. Double-click its row text string and rename it to exactly "World". 5. Right-click directly onto that new "World" root node row -> click "Add Child Node...". In the pop-up search filter prompt text box, type "Node3D". Double-click "Node3D" from the list selection rows, then double-click its text row label in the main panel and rename it to exactly "WorldGenerator". 6. Right-click onto the "World" root node row again -> click "Add Child Node...". In the search bar box, type "CharacterBody3D". Double-click it from the list rows, then double-click its text label and rename it to exactly "Player". 7. Right-click your newly spawned "Player" node row -> click "Add Child Node...". Search for "MeshInstance3D" and double-click to add it. Move your cursor pointer straight over to the far right-hand "Inspector" panel dashboard layout. Locate the "Mesh" property parameter row (which currently reads ""), click the white drop-down arrow selection box, and click "New BoxMesh" right now. This builds the physical player character body cube shape inside the local cache blocks. 8. Right-click the "Player" node row again -> click "Add Child Node...". Search for "CollisionShape3D" and add it. In the right-hand Inspector window layout, click the box next to "Shape" (currently reading ""), click the drop-down arrow, and select "New BoxShape3D". This establishes the player physical boundary fence matrix. 9. Right-click the "Player" node row one final time -> click "Add Child Node...". Search for "Camera3D" and add it. Select the Camera3D node row, look down into the center viewport grid workspace screen canvas, grab the blue transform translation handle arrow, and drag the camera layout lens slightly upward and backward along the Z-axis line so it is backed out of the player block mesh face. 10. Now, move your cursor pointer back to the top-left Scene tree panel. Left-click directly onto your "WorldGenerator" node row to highlight it active. Click the tiny "Attach Script" button icon (the sheet of paper with a green plus symbol) located right at the top left edge bar layout of the node list matrix window. Leave the path set to "res://world_generator.gd" and smash the "Create" button. 11. The main central screen text editor panel layout sheet will slide open. Highlight every single default boilerplate code text line inside the tab window (Ctrl + A) and press Delete to clear the terminal canvas entirely. 12. Copy and paste this exact full monolithic procedural block terrain generation script text straight into the empty "world_generator.gd" editor frame layout panel: ```gdscript extends Node3D var block_mesh = BoxMesh.new() var render_distance = 12 # 12x12 chunk grid size running smoothly at 60FPS velocity var block_size = 2.0 func _ready(): generate_world() func generate_world(): var multimesh = MultiMesh.new() # The updated Godot 4 enum parameter property format identifier constant! multimesh.transform_format = MultiMesh.TRANSFORM_3D multimesh.instance_count = (render_distance * 2) * (render_distance * 2) * 6 multimesh.mesh = block_mesh var index = 0 for x in range(-render_distance, render_distance): for z in range(-render_distance, render_distance): # Use mathematical sine-wave noise calculation to spawn automatic valleys and hills! var height = floor(sin(x * 0.25) * cos(z * 0.25) * 3.0) for y in range(height - 2, height + 1): if index < multimesh.instance_count: var pos = Transform3D(Basis(), Vector3(x * block_size, y * block_size, z * block_size)) multimesh.set_instance_transform(index, pos) index += 1 var mm_instance = MultiMeshInstance3D.new() mm_instance.multimesh = multimesh add_child(mm_instance) ``` 13. Now, move your cursor pointer back to the top-left Scene tree panel rows. Left-click directly onto your "Player" node row to highlight it active. Click the "Attach Script" button icon at the top left edge bar layout of the window. Leave the path set to "res://player.gd" and smash the "Create" button. 14. Clear out the entire text editor tab canvas (Ctrl + A then Delete) and copy-paste this exact full kinematic movement script straight into the "player.gd" panel box layout: ```gdscript extends CharacterBody3D const SPEED = 5.0 const JUMP_VELOCITY = 4.5 # Automatically fetch the engine gravity constant from the project registry! var gravity = ProjectSettings.get_setting("physics/3d/default_gravity") @onready var camera = $Camera3D var mouse_sensitivity = 0.002 func _ready(): # Input capture protocol to hide your mouse cursor inside the 3D game viewport! Input.set_mouse_mode(Input.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED) func _unhandled_input(event): # Trackpad and mouse look vector rotation calculations! if event is InputEventMouseMotion and Input.get_mouse_mode() == Input.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED: rotate_y(-event.relative.x * mouse_sensitivity) camera.rotate_x(-event.relative.y * mouse_sensitivity) camera.rotation.x = clamp(camera.rotation.x, deg_to_rad(-80), deg_to_rad(80)) func _physics_process(delta): # Add the real-time gravity loops to drop your block onto the terrain! if not is_on_floor(): velocity.y -= gravity * delta # Handle the Spacebar jumping kinematics! if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept") and is_on_floor(): velocity.y = JUMP_VELOCITY # Get the input direction vectors based on W, A, S, D layout values! var input_dir = Input.get_vector("ui_left", "ui_right", "ui_up", "ui_down") var direction = (transform.basis * Vector3(input_dir.x, 0, input_dir.y)).normalized() if direction: velocity.x = direction.x * SPEED velocity.z = direction.z * SPEED else: velocity.x = move_toward(velocity.x, 0, SPEED) velocity.z = move_toward(velocity.z, 0, SPEED) move_and_slide() ``` 15. Hit Ctrl + S on your laptop keyboard layout to force-save all project script parameters. Name the master scene file "world.tscn" inside your resource virtual path root repository (res://) and click Save. 16. Now, smash the giant "Play Scene" function key option button layout (F5) right at the top right header menu bar layout. A small alert popup prompt window will materialize on your screen saying "No main scene has ever been defined". Left-click that left button option that says "Select Current" to hard-link the file path. 17. OBSERVED BEHAVIOR: The standalone application gameplay window will launch, but it will instantly freeze into a completely flat, featureless zero-block blank canvas layout. Move your cursor straight down to the bottom console rows inside the Godot editor and click the "Debugger" tab. The "Errors" badge loop counter column will instantly spike and spam over 3,000 critical thread-allocation exceptions per second: "CreateJob: Jolt Physics job system exceeded the maximum number of jobs. This should not happen. Please report this. Waiting for jobs to become available..." 18. EXPECTED BEHAVIOR: The MultiMeshInstance3D matrix loop should handle drawing the geometric instanced transformations smoothly at full fluid 60FPS velocity without flooding the background worker registers of the Jolt Physics kernel pool. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [lol.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27900778/lol.zip)
